stances.claim: Leni's defining authority as a mother was 'quiet' -- non-overbearing, non-strict, non-in-your-face -- embodied in patience, kindness, and reasoning with children rather than yelling.
stances.rhetorical_move: Yields to daughter Celine's voice; CJ amplifies by selection and arrangement rather than authorial assertion.

stances.claim: Monthly allowances were a deliberate banking lesson -- children either ran out and learned to borrow (with installment paybacks) or saved and were rewarded by Leni still providing essentials like pajamas anyway.
stances.rhetorical_move: Anecdote-as-pedagogy: small domestic detail framed as life-skill formation.

stances.claim: Leni's AIM career -- earning the MBM degree in 1971 in a male-dominated pioneer batch and teaching for 37 years -- demonstrates that excellence in motherhood and graduate education are not mutually exclusive.
stances.rhetorical_move: Inspirational framing via Mari Sison Garcia: 'if Leni can do it, I certainly (could).'

stances.claim: Within the BLD Council of Servant Leaders, the worship dynamic was a complementary partnership -- CJ Art introducing the 'joyful and animated format,' Leni serving as his anchor in her reserved nature.
stances.rhetorical_move: Closes Mari's eulogy with the husband-wife dynamic from a fellow community member's vantage.

notable_anecdotes.description: Celine's monthly-allowance reconstruction: '12-year-old on the first of the month' relative bonanza, some children running out before month-end and starving while learning how banking worked, with Leni allowing borrowing against next month's allowance paid in installments; when Archie saved his money instead of buying needed pajamas, Mom bought him pajamas anyway -- 'somehow, Ate Len and I didn't learn that trick.'
notable_anecdotes.purpose: Concrete domestic-pedagogy anecdote preserving the family's signature life-lesson method.

notable_anecdotes.description: Rafa's catalog of Lola Leni's standard greetings at the Dasma house: 'How are you?' / 'How's school?' / 'Do you want chicheria? Just get, just get, we have plenty!' with the close runner-up 'Do you have a girlfriend na?'
notable_anecdotes.purpose: Preserves the verbatim affectionate register of a Filipino grandmother.

notable_anecdotes.description: Lola Leni taught Rafa to curl his tongue, play Uno, Old Maid, and Sudoku -- but never figured out the double-eyebrow raise; her phone-collecting hobby (Bounce was Rafa's favorite game on her phones) is credited as the seed of Rafa's tech career.
notable_anecdotes.purpose: Multi-generational transmission anecdote: grandmother's pastime becoming grandson's vocation.

notable_anecdotes.description: Mari Sison Garcia's recollection: Leni was 'one of four women' in AIM's male-dominated pioneering batch of 1971, balancing 'the demands of the Harvard's case study method and being mother to her five children, and a good wife to CJ Art' -- earning her MBM and becoming a 'First Fruits of AIM' alumna.
notable_anecdotes.purpose: Anchors the AIM trajectory in named-batch context.

one_paragraph_summary: A week after publishing his own eulogy for Elenita 'Leni' Carpio-Panganiban (C43, Apr. 17, 2023), CJ Panganiban yields his column space to three of the ten eulogies delivered during her wake -- selecting voices that portray Leni as mother, grandmother, and professor for 37 years at the Asian Institute of Management. Daughter Celine Panganiban-Hannett recalls 'quiet authority' parenting that never yelled, that reasoned at the 'age of reason' (eight), and that turned monthly allowances into a banking lesson -- with siblings either running out and learning installment borrowing, or saving and being rewarded by Leni still buying the pajamas Archie had skipped. Grandson Rafa Panganiban Yaptangco preserves Lola Leni's verbatim greetings at the Dasmariñas house ('Do you want chicheria? Just get, just get, we have plenty!' and 'Do you have a girlfriend na?'), her tutorials in tongue-curling and Uno and Old Maid and Sudoku, and the phone-game hobby (Bounce on her latest device) that Rafa credits as the seed of his tech career. AIM classmate and later co-professor Mari Sison Garcia situates Leni in the male-dominated pioneer batch of 1971 -- 'one of four women' -- who balanced 'the Harvard's case study method' with mothering five children and supporting CJ Art, earning their MBM as 'First Fruits of AIM,' later reuniting as faculty colleagues exchanging encouragement over lunches, and finally serving together in the Bukas Loob Sa Diyos Council of Servant Leaders, where 'CJ Art changed the dynamics of worship and Leni remained his anchor.' The column functions as curated family-and-community memorial in the voices of those who loved her most.
